Max fails to address the machine learning aspect of agentic AI that makes Claude unique vs historic productivity gains he mentions. Machine learning means that as you train AI to help you be more productive, you are training that same machine to replace you. Its not hard for a boss to learn to write prompts that do the job in v 2.0 that you trained it to do in v 1.0. All the productivity gains you make (520% in a year) are transferrable to your boss via AI skills. If you don't have those skills in a walled garden and you are the gatekeeper, then you trained that platform and anyone in the world has access for free in future releases... ATMs, autopilots and elevator operators didn't work like that... Its a new paradigm.

Really appreciate your balanced view on things as always. Favourite part of this though was your mention of the joy (or satisfaction) of being deeply involved in problem-solving or refactoring and the feeling of achievement that comes with it. I think naturally we want to get absorbed in 'deep work' for some of our day - the days when I'm not able to do this, and I'm torn between projects, meetings and piecemeal admin, I tend to end the day a lot more tired and stressed, even if the work itself is less challenging on paper. That's because your brain often craves that bit of extra stimulation, and context-switching takes more out of you. That's the risk we take with AI tooling as well, as it can distance us from the work and problem-solving. I think it's worth stating as well that this isn't just about enjoyment, but using these tools without care an easily weaken a developer's problem-solving mental muscles, which need that practice - and I think this could end up leading to a loss of productivity and developer frustration if that trend continues unchecked.
